why: The only close call is the Axiom event. Its theorem concerns M_α(p)-regularity, a strictly weaker truncated property that regular primes satisfy but which does not imply regularity; a density-one statement for a superset gives no lower bound on the density of regular primes and produces no regular prime, so it moves no quantity the statement names. That makes it a variant (a changed, weaker question), not a bound; the competing reading (same Bernoulli-divisibility mechanism) is a heuristic link, not a moved quantity. Its AI role is generated: the authors state AxiomProver produced the proof with no human assistance. Hart–Harvey–Ong is a finite computation (instances). The FLT formalisations (Best et al., Anthropic) formalise known theorems and say nothing about regular primes' infinitude or density (none); Anthropic's AI work is formalisation of a human proof, and in any case not mathematics on this problem. Qin and Guo–Tao are Vandiver-type eigenspace results (variants); Qin's year-only 2024 date cannot be placed against 26 January.
